claim_en: AN OPERATOR-LEVEL DISTINCTION IS CARRIED AS LAW. The chain rules that every occurrence of 'God SPOKE' (dibber) introduces a NEW COMMANDMENT, as against the weaker 'said' (amar) - and our 8:15 is the exhibit: the new law it introduces is the prohibition of a limb taken from a living animal. The distinction the machine draws between two speech operators is thereby a legal one, not a stylistic one.

check.note: A distinction between two speech-verb operators carried as a rule about which one installs law, with this unit's verse as the stated exhibit.

middah: M-09 (spoke against said — every spoke a new command; Jerusalem Talmud Makkot 2:6)

claim_en: THE EXIT COMMAND CARRIES A WRITTEN-AND-READ PAIR THAT ENCODES RELUCTANCE. At our 8:17 the text is written הוֹצֵא (hotze, 'bring out') and read הַיְצֵא (haitze) - both forms standing in the ink - and the chain reads the pair as the difference between bringing out and COERCING out, the man's reluctance written into the verse's own double form. The same verse's 'teem ON THE EARTH' is read as ending the ark-abstinence: procreation resumes only outside.

check.note: A written-and-read pair read as encoding the addressee's reluctance; both forms verified present in the ink at derivation.

middah: ink (the written-and-read pair bring-out / coerce-out; the reluctance reading beside)

claim_en: MORTALITY INSIDE THE ARK IS READ OFF A PLURAL. Our 8:19 says they emerged 'after their KINDS' - and R. Yochanan reads their kinds, not THEM: some of the animals that boarded died within the year and it was their descendants that emerged. The husbandry regime behind the manifest is described in testimony - day-feeders fed by day, night-feeders by night, one creature fed on worms deliberately bred in bran.

check.note: A population change inside the vessel inferred from the emergence roster's own wording.

middah: plain (the plural suffix read — their kinds, not them; Sanhedrin 108b)

claim_en: THE ALTAR OPERATOR HAS A DISPUTED CELEBRANT AND SUPPLIES A VOCABULARY ANCHOR. The chain records that the lion maimed him at the exit, leaving him unfit to sacrifice, so that SHEM offered in his place - the altar act reassigned. And our 8:20's 'of every PURE animal' is the biblical anchor for calling kosher animals 'pure', cited as such inside the impurity discussions.

check.note: A celebrant reassigned by an injury the chain supplies, and a technical vocabulary anchored at this verse.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE AROMA OPERATOR IS READ AS APPEASEMENT, AND THEN RANKED. Our 8:21's sequence - He smelled the pleasing aroma, then said He would not curse again - is read as appeasement achieved through smell, with smell held as potent as eating. The offering is then compared with Israel's later offerings and proven the lesser, since of Israel's it is said 'MY pleasing aroma YOU SHALL KEEP' - a command to repeat, which this one never received.

check.note: A sensory operator read as causing the decree's reversal, and its offering ranked against a later book's by the presence of a command to repeat.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE DOUBLED CLAUSE IS READ AS OATH FORCE, AND THE YOUTH-CLAUSE GROUNDS A PRACTICAL LAW. 'I will not continue... I will not continue' at our 8:21 is read as carrying the force of an oath rather than mere repetition. And 'the inclination of man's heart is evil FROM HIS YOUTH' is the stated basis of a concrete ruling about a toddler's excrement, with a defective-spelling parse reading the word as 'from his awakening' - that is, from birth. The heart-token opens a census: the wicked are ruled BY their hearts, the righteous rule theirs.

check.note: A doubled clause read as an oath, and a descriptive clause grounding a practical purity ruling.

middah: E10 (the doubled I-will-not-continue as oath force — Bereshit Rabbah 34:10)

claim_en: OUR 8:22 IS READ AS A MACHINE WITH A TERMINATION CONDITION AND A CHANGED WORLD-STATE. The seasons-covenant is read as enduring only WHILE THE EARTH ENDURES, so the guarantee is conditional and its annulment is discussed in two versions. And R. Acha reads the clause as installing conditions that did not exist before: because the flood generation sowed once in forty years and never buried children, seasons, fever and predators are introduced afterwards - the verse read as changing the world's operating parameters, not merely restoring them.

check.note: A covenant operator read as conditional on a termination clause, and as installing new world parameters rather than restoring old ones.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE CLOCK-CLAUSE READ ONTO ITS ADDRESSEES AS STANDING LAW. Resh Lakish: a gentile who kept a full day of rest is liable — ויום ולילה לא ישבתו ('and day and night they shall not CEASE,' Gen 8:22) read on the sons of Noach themselves; the liability rides Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's principle (their prohibition is their death-liability, Sanhedrin 57a:12), and Ravina sharpens the scope to any full day of rest, even a Monday — ceasing, not Shabbat's date. The Noahide exam's one clean class-C hole (finding F-014).

check.note: A liability rule read out of the seasons-covenant clause, seated beside its termination-condition reading.

middah: plain (the not-cease clause read on its addressees as standing law — Sanhedrin 58b)
